title: Unicon grading verdict
description: What the harness writes to object storage at the end of a job, and the only durable record of a grading run. It repeats the Forgejo identity of both the submission and the task so results can be matched back after a loss of the Unicon database, without rejudging everything.

then.description: The plan ran to the end, so the result fields carry the result and there is no error to report.

else.description: Nobody graded, or the submission itself failed. There is a sentence for a human and no verdict to record.

schema_version.description: The verdict shape this file is written against.

judging_id.description: The judgings row this result belongs to, copied from the envelope.

stage.description: Grading stage, copied from the envelope.

attempt.description: Attempt number, copied from the envelope.

task_published_tag.description: The tag on the task repo whose published plan produced this result. Two results on the same submission with different tags were graded against different tests.

outcome.description: Who owns the failure. verdict: the plan ran to the end, so read verdict and score. contestant_error: the submission did not compile, crashed or ran out of time, which is a normal result. system_error: the harness could not grade at all, for example a schema_version it does not speak or storage it could not reach, and staff should look.

verdict.description: The workflow's own word for the result, for example AC or WA. Unicon does not define the vocabulary, it displays it. Null when the outcome is not a verdict.

score.description: The workflow's score, carried as text: an optional minus sign, one or more digits, and an optional fractional part after a single dot. No exponent, no thousands separator, no leading plus. A string and not a number because JSON numbers are binary floats: a decimal score would not survive the round trip byte for byte, and a leaderboard that disagrees with the number the contestant was shown is a protest. The backend parses it once into the numeric column the leaderboard sorts on and keeps this text as written.

metrics.description: Whatever the workflow measured beyond the score, for example accuracy or peak memory. Keys and value types belong to the workflow, so this object is open.

summary.description: The per-test table the task page shows. An empty array when the workflow has no per-test structure, for example a single-metric evaluation; null only when there is no verdict at all.

started_at.description: When the harness accepted the envelope.

finished_at.description: When the harness finished the last step.

error_message.description: One sentence for a human when outcome is not verdict. Null otherwise.

submission.description: The Forgejo identity of what was graded, copied from the envelope.

org.description: Forgejo organisation that owns the submission repo.

repo.description: The contestant's submission repo for one task.

tag.description: The protected tag that is the submission. May contain a slash.

commit.description: Full commit sha the tag points at. Forgejo repos are SHA-1 today, so 40 hex characters.

task.description: The Forgejo identity of the task repo this result was graded against, copied from the envelope. Without it the published tag below names nothing: DATA-MAP.md keeps the link from a judging to its task in the Unicon database, and this file is what has to be readable when that database is gone.

org.description: Forgejo organisation that owns the task repo, the same org the submission repo is in.

repo.description: The task repo, the one carrying task.yaml and the tests.

test_result.description: One row of the per-test table.

id.description: The test's name as the task repo spells it.

verdict.description: The workflow's word for this test.

time_ms.description: Wall clock for this test, or null when the step was not measured. Explicitly null rather than absent, so an absent measurement is a statement and not an oversight.

memory_kb.description: Peak memory for this test, or null when the step was not measured.

message.description: The checker's note, shown next to the row when the stage allows it.
